title: Fail Closed When a Batch Violates Quality
objective: Put quality checks between staging and consumer-facing publish so a bad batch leaves the warehouse at last-good, quarantines the reject, and logs the failed check under a run id.
whyThisMatters: A pipeline that publishes partial or invalid data and 'fixes it later' trains consumers to distrust the warehouse. Fail closed: last-good stays queryable, the reject is inspectable, and the next good batch can publish.
evidence: The check definitions (freshness, volume band, null rate or unexpected values) in code or config
Before and after queries on the consumer-facing table around a failing batch
A structured log line for the failed check that includes run_id and check name
The quarantine table or file showing rejected rows or the rejected batch id with a reason
Captured counts proving a later good batch published after the failure
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: A batch that fails a named check leaves the consumer-facing warehouse table's row count or max(updated_at) unchanged, shown by captured before and after queries.
The failing check name and a run_id appear in a structured log line that parses as JSON or a documented key=value format.
Rejected rows or the rejected batch id appear in a quarantine table or file with a reason column or field populated.
A subsequent good batch publishes successfully after the failed one, shown by captured counts that change only on the good run.
